standing: Root/coauthor source assent to one bounded checker correction. Fresh independent acceptance of successor18 still required.

findingDispositions.finding: Ten defaulting expected-refusal comparisons can falsely pass an unexpected null-detail exception.
findingDispositions.correction: Each handler now requires its exact expected-refusal key to be present before comparing the detail. Deliberate null, named detail, error-code and remedy checks retain their existing meanings.

original.finding: When the new guard fires, the third `check(...)` argument is still `r.detail`, which is None in exactly the detail-free case the guard exists to catch, so the failure row reads detail: null. My injected run shows precisely that: {'id': 'repair.preview-applicable', 'ok': False, 'detail': None}.
original.whyNotRequired: The check ID identifies the failing case, the verdict is correct, and changing the diagnostic argument would touch the same ten lines without altering any verdict. The corpus already carries the better pattern (expectRemedyContains) for the three explicit-null cases.
original.suggestionForAFuturePass: Consider passing a non-null diagnostic such as the error code or remedy when the expectation key is absent. Not proposed here; out of bounded scope.

nonBlockingObservation.disposition: V18-OBS-1 null diagnostic remains nonblocking: caseID identifies the failed control, correct failure is emitted. Optional richer reference-test diagnostics require no public design change; preserve observation as future convenience, not unperformed qualification.
